text: When you build a REST API, good design makes it easier for others to use. Start by choosing clear, meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers understand what each one does. Always return the correct status codes, for example 200 for success, 404 when something is missing, and 500 for server errors. Write clear documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and its responses. It is also important to use versioning, such as /v1/users, so older applications keep working when you make changes. These simple practices help your API stay reliable, consistent, and easy to maintain over time.
